what_this_is: The task-level arm for static YaRN at FACTOR 2.0 and a 524,288 window, run on the 47 pre-registered discriminating tasks (receipts/tb21-512k-preregistration.json). PARTIAL BY DESIGN: I stopped it deliberately with 10 tasks still in flight to pause the 8x host, because the balance had fallen to $4.88 and the marginal value of 4 more tasks was far below the value of buying closeout runway.

completion.why_partial_is_still_valid: the comparison below is restricted to the 37 tasks this arm actually completed, and the other two arms are re-scored on exactly those 37, so the denominators match. Cancelling 10 tasks costs statistical power, not validity.

headline: At factor 2.0 the YaRN penalty is INVISIBLE at task level: 20/37 for 512k-YaRN against 20/37 for 262k-native, an exact tie. At factor 4.0 the same subset scores 11/37. So the fidelity cost measured at the token level - 4.23e-03 for factor 2.0 versus 1.03e-02 for factor 4.0 - shows up at task level as 'no detectable difference' versus 'nine tasks lost out of thirty-seven'.

512k_vs_native.reading: 2 lost, 2 gained - pure churn, exactly what single-pass variance produces. No evidence of any task-level cost from factor 2.0.
512k_vs_native.p_value_note: A two-sided sign test on a perfectly symmetric 2-versus-2 split is p = 1.0 by definition. My first computation printed 1.375 because the naive two-sided doubling double-counts the central term when the split is even; a probability above 1 is arithmetically impossible and is corrected here rather than left in the receipt.

512k_vs_1M.reading: 12 versus 3 discordant, sign test p = 0.03516. This is the one comparison in the family that reaches conventional significance, and it is the one with the largest underlying token-level difference, which is the consistency one would hope for.

two_scales_agree.reading: the token-level and task-level instruments were built independently, use different data, and agree: factor 2.0 is cheap enough to disappear into single-pass noise, factor 4.0 is not.

confounds_and_limits: PARTIAL: 10 of 47 tasks were cancelled by me, so power is reduced. The comparison is restricted to the 37 completed and the other arms re-scored on the same 37.

The 262k and 1M arms ran at C32 and C16 respectively; this arm ran C32. Where it is compared to the 1M arm the concurrency differs, and less contention favours the 1M arm, so the +9 is if anything understated.
All three arms are single pass, so all carry best-of-1 variance; the 2-lost/2-gained churn against native is that variance made visible.
n=37 on a deliberately DISCRIMINATING subset, not a random sample of the suite. The subset was chosen to be hard, so none of these fractions is comparable to any published x/89 figure.
Denominator is 37. Never quote this as a Terminal-Bench score: the subset is selective and the agent timeout is non-stock.
does_not_revise: 44/89 best-of-2 stock clock (the published lower bound)
